# rework_claims_r3 — gap_waiver_cancellations_and_claims (policy-task audit revision_2)

- C9 (bn_floor_value acting only through bn_value_floor's tier): closed. The value floor is now a baseline quantity of the worksheet benefit. The baseline states that the actual cash value deducted is the larger of the insurer's ACV and the value floor, at a default percent of the book value at origination. bn_value_floor sets the percent (its fall-through equals the default), and bn_floor_value sets the vehicle value the floor is figured on (its fall-through is the book value). Each factor changes a quantity the baseline already has. With the other factor at its baseline, each one still moves the task-0 result. The old combination sentence that named both factors' quantities is gone.
- C10 (same-day tie unstated): closed charter-wide. Every policy now states the tie for its latest-claim read (latest reporting date; on a same-date tie, the claim recorded first). The two reimbursement policies and both excluded totals state it for the latest accepted proof (latest review date; recorded first on a tie). The starting balance states it for the latest due-date change, cap-applied and cap-ended records. Both excluded totals state it for the latest cap-applied, cap-ended and extension records. In the excluded totals, the latest premium is now the premium whose billing period starts latest, never one picked by billing date. The rule says a backdated placement bills two or more premiums on one day while no two premiums share a billing period. The billing-date read now selects by billing-period start, so every read of "the latest premium" uses one row.
- R2-O1 (Premier past-due day limits that never exclude): closed. The Premier past-due relief is by count alone (one: none counted; two: one counted; three or more: all). The vacuous 30/75-day conditions and their parameters are removed. The Plus limits (20/60), which do bite, are unchanged.
- R2-O3 ("refund due" netting only the latest premium): closed. The pending-refund tier of both placed-premium factors now applies only when the accepted proof's effective date falls within the latest premium's billing period. In that case the latest premium's share is the whole refund the collateral protection terms leave due. A proof whose coverage starts before the latest billing period, with its refund not yet credited, falls to the gross tier, and the rule says so. The capitalised-premium replaced_by sentences were reworded to match ("net of refunds credited or, where the proof's coverage starts inside the latest billing period, due").
- O6 (post-loss late charges in the fee part): closed. In both excluded totals the fee part is the fees due less the late charges assessed on installments that fell due after the date of loss, never below 0.00. Compute reads those charges from the contract ledger by the installment due date each charge names. Compute locates those installments on the contract's monthly due-day sequence by whole months from the next due date (months to today less months to the date of loss), which equals "due after the date of loss" whether or not the borrower was behind at the loss. Probes are in plan.md.
- C1 / C4 (reimbursement filler shares; factor floor): NOT closed. pd/ud keep their round-2 factor sets this round, so the gate block stays green. This is not a claim of compliance. Analysis:
  - Option (b) is unavailable on the frozen blueprint. The gap schema's only borrower act with a number is on the claim row. gap_cancellation_requests holds no numeric field. A gap_refund_issued row is the company's act, and its only trigger-free disposition is mailed_to_borrower. Task 0's draw (three prerequisites, four computing problems) also needs all four computable claim-row fields, so dropping the reimbursement leaves no fourth write in a claim tree.
  - Option (a) has a ceiling. The reimbursement is a lower-of over caps on one deducted figure, and in a lower-of only the binding cap moves the result. Several factors bear weight together only as selections inside one cap, as timeliness gates, or as a raised cap above a stricter standard. Five real, record-driven candidates exist:
    - which accepted proof was in force on the date of loss (method);
    - which coverage's deductible applies (method);
    - the reimbursement-claim window start, measured from the settlement as the claim report evidences it (method);
    - the window length (parameter);
    - SCRA tolling of the window (parameter; cross-difficulty).
    Of these, the window length has the weakest partition (by loss type). That gives five for Premier where the draw needs six. The alternative, the starting balance taking six, fails too: the frozen measure fixes interest to the date of loss and "no extension deferrals", so it leaves no further real convention. Plus can carry four of the five.
  - Ruling requested: whether the timeliness family counts as real GAP terms for the reimbursement, and how task 0's sixth Premier factor (or the starting balance's two) is to be met.
- Sweep: design_rationale (both tasks), factor traces, the plain recomputations, computations and evaluation tracing were regenerated from the new compute. The probe table in plan.md was extended.
